The extinction of the dinosaurs, approximately 66 million years ago, is primarily attributed to the impact of a giant asteroid near what is now the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico, along with volcanic eruptions and climate changes. This catastrophic event significantly affected the Earth's environment, leading to the collapse of ecosystems.

The most widely accepted cause of the extinction of the dinosaurs is a catastrophic asteroid impact near present-day Yucatan, Mexico, around 66 million years ago, leading to significant climate change and disruption of ecosystems. Other contributing factors may include intense volcanic activity and changes in sea levels.
